run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T05:26:51Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend is explained by a brief, total loss of the ad service's serving endpoint. At 2026-11-17T05:25:40-05:25:43 Deployment ad in namespace otel-demo was rolled out (new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5, old pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq killed) and the pod-template annotation shows this was a kubectl rollout restart. The replacement pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz was marked Ready at 05:25:43 although its container has no readiness, liveness or startup probe and its only log line before 05:48 is 'Ad service starting.' at 05:29:53. From 05:26:51 frontend's calls to grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds failed fail-fast (about 88% under 2 ms) with tcp.connect error spans and dns.lookup spans, and ad served zero GetAds spans until about 05:37:30. Those ad-call failures equal, window for window, the errors on GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and GET, which is what drove frontend's error rate (150 error spans in the 5m window evaluated at 05:26:51, consistent with the alert's 2.3556% reading). Errors ended by 05:37:51 as ad traffic resumed and successful tcp.connect spans appeared. What triggered the rollout restart and why the new ad process needed roughly 12 minutes to accept connections are not established (change_history is not integrated, Jaeger returned no traces for these services, and no kube-state-metrics series exist), so the conclusion is partial. frontend itself was never restarted and its other dependencies show no comparable error increase.

claims.text: frontend error spans were 0 until the evaluation at 05:26:51, when 150 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans appeared in the preceding 5 minutes; they stayed elevated (peak 1015.6 spans per 5m at 05:29:51) and returned to 0 at 05:37:51. The affected operations were grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, GET and tcp.connect, and the per-window error counts along the GetAds -> /api/data -> GET chain are identical (for example 252.22 each at 05:35:51).

frontend's dns.lookup spans exist only during the error window (1.11 per 5m at 05:26:51 rising to 8.89, back to 0 at 05:38:51); tcp.connect STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans appear in the same window (7.78 at 05:26:51 up to 12.22 at 05:28:51-05:29:51, then 0 by 05:37:51), while tcp.connect STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans (successful connects) appear only at 05:37:51-05:38:51.

The failing frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds spans are fail-fast, not timeouts: in the 5m window ending 05:35:00 there were 176.44 error spans, of which 155.36 were <=2 ms, 163.12 <=4 ms, 164.23 <=10 ms, 174.22 <=100 ms and 176.44 <=1000 ms.

The ad service's own span volume for oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds collapsed to zero during the same interval: 208.89 spans per 5m at 05:26:51, 144.74, 86.67, 32.22 at 05:29:51, then 0 for the evaluations ending 05:30:51 through 05:37:51, resuming at 70.36 at 05:38:51. No ad-side error spans were recorded, and ad's GetAds latency before the incident was low (258.89 spans in the 5m ending 05:20:00, of which 206.67 were <=2 ms and all <=1000 ms).

In namespace otel-demo at 05:25:40-05:25:43 the events are exactly an ad Deployment rollout: Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1', ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 created pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, that pod was Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started (container ad started 05:25:42), then 'Stopping container ad' on ad-554b849958-gcmfq, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 'Deleted pod', and Deployment ad 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0'. No Unhealthy, BackOff, Failed or Evicted events for ad are present.

The new ad ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:25:40Z, while its container image (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), env vars, ports and resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi) are identical to the previous ReplicaSet ad-554b849958, so the application spec did not change.

Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz on node i-00afa9d1463304f93 reports condition Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 2026-11-17T05:25:43Z, container ad running since 05:25:42 with restartCount 0, and its container spec has readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null. Its only log line between 05:20:00 and 05:48:20 is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-17T05:29:53.903167388Z, and no previous container instance exists.

frontend-proxy recorded its own error spans concurrently: ingress errors rose from a 0-3.3 per 5m baseline to 35.56 at 05:27:00, peaked at 253.33 at 05:31:00 and were 0 from 05:40:00; 'router frontend egress' errors follow the same shape (35.56 at 05:27:00, peak 252.22). frontend-proxy's error count in the 5m window ending 05:26:51 was 71.11, against a 1-6 per 5m baseline earlier in the window.

frontend itself was not restarted: pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 has been running since 2026-11-17T04:53:15Z with restartCount 0. Within the by-operation data for frontend, the grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error series is the one that rose during the incident while the cart, checkout, product-catalog and recommendation call series show no error values.

Current cluster state shows a configured path from frontend to ad: Service ad (clusterIP 100.64.219.118) selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad and maps port 8080 to targetPort 8080, and Endpoints ad contains only address 100.96.1.122 pointing at pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz on port 8080.

Node-level causes are not supported: all 5 nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False, and the node hosting the new ad pod (i-00afa9d1463304f93) also hosts the accounting, currency, kafka, product-catalog and shipping pods, whose services did not show error increases during the ad outage.

The current flagd-config (ConfigMap flagd-config, key demo.flagd.json) has adFailure defaultVariant 'off', adHighCpu 'off', adManualGc 'on', and all other declared fault flags (cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage) 'off'.

Clustered events also include unrelated data-recorders namespace activity (Job Completed and SuccessfulCreate, PersistentVolumeClaim Provisioning/ExternalProvisioning, StatefulSet SuccessfulCreate) plus one PersistentVolume VolumeFailedDelete; these are in a different namespace and involve no otel-demo workload. The only otel-demo Deployment and ReplicaSet events in the window are the ad rollout, with none for frontend or frontend-proxy.

Mechanism: the rollout restart removed the only serving ad pod at 05:25:43 while the replacement pod had already joined the Service endpoints as Ready (no readiness or startup probe exists to hold it back), so frontend's gRPC channel to ad:8080 was refused; the fail-fast error durations plus the tcp.connect errors, with successful connects appearing only at 05:37:51, match a connection-refused path rather than slow responses.

The new ad container needed roughly 12 minutes to accept connections (Ready at 05:25:43, only 'Ad service starting.' at 05:29:53, first successful frontend tcp.connect at about 05:37:51), plausibly because the JVM cold start runs under a 50m CPU / 450Mi memory limit; no container CPU-throttling or start-latency metric is available to confirm this.

frontend-proxy's ingress and 'router frontend egress' error spans rose and fell with frontend's own error spans at comparable magnitude, so they are most plausibly the proxied error responses from frontend rather than an independent proxy fault; the proxy's internal state is not otherwise evidenced.

The enabled fault-injection setting adManualGc='on' ('Triggers full manual garbage collections in the ad service') is a candidate that does not match the observed failure path: ad served no GetAds requests at all while frontend's calls failed fail-fast at the connection level, and ad's pre-incident GetAds durations were low, so this flag is not shown to have caused the outage.

An enabled ad-service failure flag in flagd-config is rejected as the cause: the current flagd-config sets adFailure to 'off', and ad produced no error spans or failed GetAds operations of its own during the outage, which a declared 'Fail ad service' fault would produce.

Node or infrastructure pressure on the node hosting the new ad pod is rejected: every node reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable False, and co-located pods (accounting, currency, kafka, product-catalog, shipping) did not show error increases.

fraud-detection changed during the wider window for another reason and is not tied to this alert: its container's last termination was OOMKilled with exitCode 137 at 2026-11-17T04:58:35Z (restartCount 1, running again since 04:58:35), about 27 minutes before the frontend error onset, and its error-span rate stayed at roughly 1.1 per 5m during the incident.

Add a readinessProbe (and startupProbe) on the ad container's gRPC port 8080 and raise the 50m CPU limit so a restarted ad pod is not published to the Service endpoints before it can serve; consider running more than one ad replica so a single-pod rollout no longer removes the only endpoint.

Confirm from the cluster audit or change-history source who issued the kubectl rollout restart recorded as kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:25:40Z on Deployment ad, since that integration is not available in this Run.

gaps: The actor and cause behind the rollout restart of Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T05:25:40Z cannot be established: change_history is not integrated in this Run and the annotation records only the timestamp.

Trace evidence is missing: traces_list_services lists both ad and frontend, but the frontend searches returned nothing (1c599508-8f1a-4408-ae8e-af2acb8be1d9-t0:e75353cf-6f80-4791-99e1-b271082e3141 for 05:26:00-05:39:00 and 3669b580-53ec-4d7b-9be1-c335f8da7aa9-t1:71f0355c-39d8-4c30-9a18-f97f3262457f for 05:42:00-05:48:20) and the ad search returned nothing (01257d0a-1f2e-4c8b-b429-6d435ed87690-t2:c841f918-cad5-4c43-b252-5fe8673f8f17), so the exact gRPC status returned to frontend is unverified and no parent-child call edges could be read.

Metric-series gaps: the rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count query and its get_series lookup returned no data (55423436-c23b-41c6-9e52-4a54686f995d-t0:b96340f7-2457-4e0a-bf0f-8914c6f64348 and 3669b580-53ec-4d7b-9be1-c335f8da7aa9-t0:5b0b6008-fcac-4d0f-8937-d8650669a4e5), so client-side gRPC status codes are unknown; kube_deployment_status_replicas_available for ad and frontend returned no data (3f3e54d5-4b43-4afa-8cfb-a73244fd2290-t1:67170ab5-d9b3-485d-bc1e-0ec7f174c772), no kube_pod_status_* series exist (3f3e54d5-4b43-4afa-8cfb-a73244fd2290-t2:e11b8e00-a80f-4809-b9ff-9f6732a4c25a), and the RequestErrorRate rule is not loaded in this Prometheus (3f3e54d5-4b43-4afa-8cfb-a73244fd2290-t0:f9288015-2294-4418-a76a-8d184bef2d2b); the ad pod's Ready=True at 05:25:43 is its state at query time (~05:50), not a historical reading.

The reason the ad container took from 05:25:42 (container start) to about 05:37:30 (first successful frontend tcp.connect) to accept connections is unknown: there is no container CPU-throttling, restart or probe metric, and the container emitted only one log line ('Ad service starting.' at 05:29:53).

flagd logs for 05:25:00-05:40:00 returned no lines for init-config, flagd or flagd-ui (c2a719c8-a278-4589-aa52-7c1a85b8d9ca-t0:73d2eb0d-5a83-414a-b984-ecca87eab59f), so the ad service's flagd initialization at startup cannot be checked, and flagd-config's current content cannot show whether the file changed around 05:25.

NetworkPolicies in namespace otel-demo returned no objects (06d1dff2-20ad-46ef-bc27-98da6c836e7f-t2:a35304f3-4489-4def-8ae8-113bdb9c4681), so a transient network-policy fault can be neither confirmed nor excluded.

Per-service error status is unknown for services whose STATUS_CODE_ERROR series were not returned in the by-service query (cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, kafka, product-catalog, quote, shipping, load-generator); an unreturned series is not a zero reading, so those services are neither confirmed affected nor confirmed error-free.
EndpointSlice history is unavailable, so whether Endpoints ad held a stale or premature address between 05:25:43 and 05:37:30 cannot be verified.
next_steps: Query the cluster audit log or change-history source for the kubectl rollout restart on Deployment otel-demo/ad at 2026-11-17T05:25:40Z and for any ConfigMap edits to flagd-config in the same minutes.
Add a readinessProbe and startupProbe on the ad container's gRPC port and re-check that a rolling restart of ad no longer removes the Service endpoint before the server listens.
Retrieve from a trace backend with longer retention the ad service's returned gRPC status and message for 05:25:43-05:37:30 to confirm what frontend received.
Measure ad container CPU throttling and cold-start duration under the current 50m limit to confirm or refute the slow-start hypothesis.
